- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 1-2% below peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be too optimistic in early days (first 5-7 days) when sentiment is positive; dampen initial forecast by 5-10%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00 → 1.00), model overfits to recent sentiment; use sentiment lag (e.g., 3-day sentiment) as smoother signal.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; add 1-2% downward bias for 10-15 day horizon.
